title: Transfers failing after payment-service v1.9 release (connection leak)
summary: Card transfers failed for 14 minutes right after payment-service v1.9 went live. Logs showed HikariPool connection timeouts and the DB pool sat at 100%.
rootCause: A refactor in v1.9 did not close database connections on the error path, leaking the pool.
resolution: Rolled back to v1.8. Added a pool-usage alert and a connection-leak test to the pipeline.

title: Connection pool too small for payday peak
summary: On payday the payment DB pool filled up and transfers slowed down. No release had gone out.
rootCause: Pool size of 50 was too small for payday traffic.
resolution: Raised pool size from 50 to 120 and added autoscaling for payment-service.

title: Ledger database failover reset all connections
summary: Planned database failover reset every connection; account-service errors for a few minutes.
rootCause: Database failover during business hours.
resolution: Waited for failover to complete, restarted consumers. Moved failovers to the maintenance window.

title: Primary card network outage, authorizations timing out
summary: Card authorizations timed out after 5 s on the primary route. The card network status page confirmed an outage.
rootCause: External outage at the primary card network, not a DemoCorp fault.
resolution: Switched card traffic to the backup processor. Added automatic failover when the primary error rate stays above 20%.

title: Card network latency spike during regional maintenance
summary: Card network latency rose to several seconds during the provider's regional maintenance.
rootCause: Provider maintenance window not announced to DemoCorp.
resolution: Moved traffic to the backup route until maintenance finished.

title: All card payments failing: card-network TLS certificate expired
summary: Every card authorization failed instantly with PKIX path validation errors.
rootCause: The client TLS certificate for the card network connection expired at midnight.
resolution: Installed the renewed certificate. Added an alert 30 days before certificate expiry.

title: Payday rush hit card processor rate limit (HTTP 429)
summary: About a third of card authorizations were rejected with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests on salary day.
rootCause: Traffic exceeded the processor's contracted quota of 2000 requests per minute.
resolution: Turned on queue-and-throttle for authorizations. Requested a higher quota before the next payday.

title: Customers charged twice after retry policy change
summary: Duplicate debits appeared after payment retries were increased. Support received many 'charged twice' tickets.
rootCause: A config change raised retries to 3 and disabled idempotency keys, so retried payments were processed again.
resolution: Reverted the retry config, refunded duplicates, and added a contract test that requires idempotency keys.

title: Good card payments declined after fraud threshold change
summary: Decline rate jumped from 3% to over 30% right after a fraud rule update.
rootCause: Fraud score threshold lowered from 0.85 to 0.40, flagging normal customers.
resolution: Restored the threshold. New fraud rules now run in shadow mode for a day first.

title: Balances not updating: ledger consumer stuck on malformed message
summary: Transfers succeeded but balances stayed the same. Ledger queue depth kept growing; logs repeated the same message id.
rootCause: A malformed (poison) ledger message with a comma decimal blocked the consumer.
resolution: Moved the message to the dead-letter queue, consumer caught up. Added a retry limit before dead-lettering.

title: Account cache down, database overloaded, balances slow
summary: Balance checks took seconds; Redis refused connections and every read went to the database.
rootCause: Account cache node crashed after a memory limit was hit.
resolution: Restarted the cache and raised its memory limit. Added a cache circuit breaker.

title: Credential-stuffing attack on login
summary: Failed logins jumped to over 20 per second from hundreds of IP addresses; several accounts were locked.
rootCause: Attackers replayed leaked username/password pairs from another site's breach.
resolution: Enabled step-up verification on login and blocked the attacking IP ranges. Added breached-password checks.

title: Partner API token used to scrape account data
summary: One open-banking partner token read hundreds of account records per second from new IP addresses.
rootCause: The partner's API token leaked from their CI logs.
resolution: Revoked the token and issued a new one with narrower scopes. Added per-token volume alerts.

title: False alarm: latency alert during nightly interest batch
summary: A latency alert fired for 40 seconds while the nightly interest batch ran. No customer impact.
rootCause: Alert threshold too sensitive during the batch window. Nothing was broken.
resolution: Closed as false positive. Raised the alert duration to 5 minutes during the batch window.

title: False alarm: flapping health check after config reload
summary: Health check flapped for a minute after a config reload. Users saw nothing.
rootCause: Health check timeout shorter than reload time.
resolution: Closed as false positive; increased health check timeout.

title: banking-api 4.0 release broke login for Android users
summary: Login errors for Android users right after banking-api 4.0 was deployed.
rootCause: New header validation rejected requests from the older Android app.
resolution: Rolled back to 3.9, fixed validation, re-released as 4.0.1.

title: account-service 3.0 migration locked the balances table
summary: Balance reads timed out after account-service 3.0 was deployed; a migration held a table lock.
rootCause: A schema migration in 3.0 took an exclusive lock on a large table.
resolution: Rolled back, re-ran the migration online during the maintenance window.

title: Payments slow because of noisy neighbour on shared database host
summary: Payment latency doubled; another team's batch job saturated the shared DB host.
rootCause: Shared database host overloaded by an unrelated batch job.
resolution: Moved the batch job to a replica.

title: Public API certificate expired, mobile app could not connect
summary: Mobile app showed connection errors; the public TLS certificate had expired.
rootCause: Certificate auto-renewal job failed silently.
resolution: Installed a new certificate and added monitoring for the renewal job.

title: Payment timeouts after connection timeout config change
summary: A config change lowered the processor timeout to 500 ms; many payments timed out.
rootCause: Timeout set lower than the processor's normal response time.
resolution: Reverted the config. Config changes now need a second reviewer.

title: Bot traffic overloaded the public balance endpoint
summary: A bot network hammered the balance endpoint, slowing the app for everyone.
rootCause: Scraping bots without rate limits on the endpoint.
resolution: Blocked the bot IP ranges and added per-client rate limits.

title: Cache eviction storm after deploy caused DB spike
summary: After a cache config change every key expired at once and the database spiked.
rootCause: All cache keys shared the same TTL.
resolution: Restarted the cache with jittered TTLs.

title: Memory leak in payment-service 1.7 caused restarts
summary: payment-service instances restarted every 20 minutes after 1.7 went live.
rootCause: An unbounded in-memory cache in 1.7 leaked memory.
resolution: Rolled back to 1.6 and bounded the cache.

title: Transaction database disk full
summary: Transfers could not be saved; the transaction database disk reached 100%.
rootCause: Audit partitions were never archived.
resolution: Archived old partitions and added a disk usage alert at 80%.

title: Clock drift broke one-time passcodes on one server
summary: Some customers' one-time passcodes were rejected; only requests hitting one server failed.
rootCause: NTP stopped on one server and its clock drifted 90 seconds.
resolution: Resynced the clock, removed the server from rotation, added NTP monitoring.

title: Runbook: payment DB connection pool exhausted
summary: If the payment DB pool is above 90% and errors mention connection timeouts, check for a release in the last 30 minutes.
rootCause: Usually a connection leak in a new release, sometimes payday load.
resolution: If a release went out: roll back. If not: check traffic and raise pool size.

title: Runbook: card network errors
summary: Timeouts on the primary route usually mean a provider outage; PKIX errors mean a certificate problem; HTTP 429 means quota.
rootCause: Provider outage, expired certificate, or rate limit.
resolution: Outage: fail over to backup. Certificate: rotate. 429: enable throttling and ask for more quota.

title: Runbook: ledger backlog growing
summary: If ledger queue depth grows and the same message id repeats in logs, a poison message is blocking the consumer.
rootCause: Malformed ledger message.
resolution: Move the message to the dead-letter queue; the consumer will catch up.

title: Runbook: login attack
summary: Failed logins above 5 per second from many IPs is a credential-stuffing attack.
rootCause: Leaked credentials being replayed.
resolution: Enable step-up verification; block the worst IP ranges; notify security.

title: Runbook: partner token abuse
summary: One partner token reading far more records than normal from new IPs is likely compromised.
rootCause: Leaked partner credential.
resolution: Revoke the token, contact the partner, issue a narrower token.
